claims.claim: Gallopamil, a close verapamil-type analog sharing the dimethoxyphenethyl-N-methyl-aminopropyl scaffold, showed 96.3% oral bioavailability in humans, supporting F >= 20% for this structural family.
Verapamil, the direct structural parent, had absolute oral bioavailability of 22% (17-29%) in fasted volunteers, which is at or above the 20% threshold.
Sustained-release verapamil gave F = 49 ± 14% fasted and 34 ± 12% fed, and cirrhosis studies reported F from 38% to 52.3%, all supporting F >= 20%.
Drotaverine, a related dimethoxy/diethoxy benzocyclic amine, had mean absolute F = 58.2 ± 18.2% with a minimum of 24.5%, supporting F >= 20%.
Other basic dimethoxyphenyl drugs, bevantolol and vernakalant, had F = 57% and 58-71%, respectively, all above the 20% threshold.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability measurement exists for the query molecule itself.
Evidence is transferred from close analogs, mainly verapamil/gallopamil and related basic dimethoxyphenyl drugs, rather than an exact-match context.
The physicochemical prior notes a low neutral fraction (0.02) and high rotatable bond count, but no direct permeability, solubility, or first-pass data are available for the query.
Formulation, dose, and food effects for the query are unspecified, so quantitative F may vary, but the available evidence does not indicate F < 20%.
content.decision_summary: All transferable L1 evidence supports F >= 20%: close analogs range from verapamil fasted F = 22% to gallopamil F = 96.3%, with most values well above threshold. No affirmative evidence supports F < 20%, so the prediction is high with moderate confidence due to analog-based transfer.
